item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Fall as Korea Chipmakers Slide Once Again
item.description: Emerging-market equities fell for the first time in three days, led down by South Korean chipmakers unwinding some of the record gains they made on Friday.

item.title: Malaysia’s Top Bank Is Said to Near Buying Ageas Stake in Etiqa
item.description: Malayan Banking Bhd. is nearing a deal to buy out Belgian insurer Ageas SA’s minority stake in Etiqa, people familiar with the matter said, a move that would help Malaysia’s biggest lender take full ownership of the Southeast Asian insurer.

item.title: US Uses Euros to Buy Yen to Avoid Weaker Dollar, Strategists Say
item.description: The US Treasury may be using euros rather than dollars to fund its yen purchases to avoid weakening its own currency and casting doubt on its strong greenback policy, according to strategists.

item.title: China’s Wu Vows Further Expansion of Market Links to Hong Kong
item.description: China is working closely with Hong Kong authorities to expand the Stock Connect cross-border trading link by adding yuan-denominated stock counters and real estate investment trusts, according China Securities Regulatory Commission Chairman Wu Qing.

item.title: Zepto Delays IPO in Latest Sign India’s Listing Boom Is Losing Momentum
item.description: Manipal Health, Indo-MIM and Juniper Green Energy have cut offer sizes to get their deals through.

item.title: Alibaba’s Qwen3.8-Max AI Model Claims Benchmark Scores Rivaling Anthropic
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. released its latest flagship AI model, with performance claims putting it alongside global leaders like Anthropic’s Fable.

item.title: Fanuc Shares Dive Most in 40 Years After Procurement Fears Hit
item.description: Fanuc Corp. shares plunged the most in four decades after the maker of factory robots raised its profit outlook by less than expected, heightening fears about soaring prices of materials.

item.title: Vietnam Trade Deficit Reaches $3.59 Billion as Imports Surge
item.description: Vietnam posted an eighth straight monthly trade deficit in July as factories continue to ramp up capacity, even as the export-reliant economy comes under renewed pressure from US tariffs.

item.title: Southeast Asia’s Factory Activity Bounces Back From 11-Month Low
item.description: Southeast Asia’s manufacturing sector rebounded in July, as growth in new orders and production accelerated to their fastest pace since the conflict in the Middle East began.

item.title: Iron Ore Hits One-Year Low on Trader Concerns and Demand Outlook
item.description: Iron ore sank to the lowest level in more than a year amid concerns about a major physical trader of the commodity, which compounded existing market softness linked to a challenging demand outlook.

item.title: China Factory Slump Reinforces Signs of Economic Slowdown
item.description: China’s manufacturing activity for export-oriented firms unexpectedly slowed in July, according to a private survey, adding to signs of economic weakness.

item.title: Chinese Government Bond Futures Kick Off Trading in Hong Kong
item.description: Chinese government bond futures began trading in Hong Kong on Monday, marking authorities’ third attempt to use the hedging tool to further open up the country’s debt market.

item.title: Japan’s Use of Fed Repo May Ease Pressure on Treasury Market
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s championing of a Federal Reserve facility Japan can use to boost the yen comes with the benefit of protecting the US bond market from excess sales.

item.title: CXMT Price Targets Are $1 Trillion Apart as Analysts Differ
item.description: CXMT Corp. is one of the most polarizing stocks in Asia, with the range of analyst opinions delineating the key arguments driving volatility in the memory-chip stock trade.

item.title: US Treasury’s Firepower for Yen Support May Be Limited, JPM Says
item.description: The US Treasury has limited liquid resources to support further coordinated currency intervention alongside Japan, though its firepower could be expanded substantially if officials resort to more extraordinary measures, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co.

item.title: Yen Bears Face Risks on Joint US-Japan Action, Strategists Say
item.description: Strategists say the coordinated intervention between Japan and the US increases the risk for anyone betting against the currency. President Donald Trump said the US joined a currency-market intervention that lifted the yen last week as a sign of friendship with Japan.

item.title: Morgan Stanley Sees 36% Upside to Korean Stocks After ‘Washout’
item.description: Morgan Stanley upgraded South Korean stocks to overweight, saying the recent “leverage washout” offers investors a better entry point into the artificial intelligence trade and industrial super-cycle theme.

item.title: AI and Chips Are Turning Malaysia Into Asia’s Growth Standout
item.description: Joel William is about to begin a feasibility study for a Chinese client weighing a chemical plant in Sarawak, Malaysia’s biggest state on the northern coast of Borneo.

item.title: Bessent, Japan Say Won’t Hesitate on More Intervention

item.title: Japanese Stocks Set to Fall on Yen Worries, Kioxia Guidance Miss
item.description: Japanese stock futures pointed to a lower open as traders remain on alert for further yen intervention after Tokyo and New York coordinated to support the currency. Kioxia Holdings Corp. may come under pressure after its profit forecast missed analysts’ expectations.

item.title: Oil Declines on Iran Deal Optimism, Yen in Focus: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil dropped and US equity-index futures rose after President Donald Trump said fresh US-Iran talks would begin Monday, boosting optimism the two sides could reach a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 3
item.description: Oil fell after US President Donald Trump said new talks with Iran would begin on Monday after he called off a planned attack on the Islamic Republic.

item.title: Bessent Says More Steps Possible on Yen as Trump Praises Japan
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the US stepped in to help fight “disorderly” movements in the yen and is ready to keep helping Japan, while President Donald Trump said the currency-market intervention was a sign of friendship with Tokyo.

item.title: Trump Says US Intervention in Yen Was ‘A Signal of Friendship’
item.description: “It was a signal of friendship,” President Donald Trump says after being asked why the US intervened to support the Japanese yen.

item.title: Rates, Housing Slump Threaten Australia’s Upbeat Profit Outlook
item.description: Australia’s resilient earnings outlook may hit a snag in the August results season as the country’s biggest companies reveal how they’re navigating a fragile economy.

item.title: Warsh Raises Rethink on Fed’s Policy Meeting Frequency, Timing
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has raised the possibility of changing the frequency of the US central bank’s regular policy meetings, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Netflix Looks to Add ‘Hot Ones’ to Its Growing Stable of YouTube Hits
item.description: Netflix has run into a small hurdle in its pursuit of top YouTube creators

item.title: AstraZeneca Said to Have Explored Bristol Myers Merger
item.description: AstraZeneca Plc has explored an acquisition of Bristol Myers Squibb Co., in a megadeal that would create one of the world’s largest drugmakers, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Prysmian Is Said Near Takeover of US Electrical Maker Atkore
item.description: Italy’s Prysmian is in advanced talks to acquire electrical manufacturing company Atkore Inc., people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Australia Expands Demand That Big Tech Pay for News Stories
item.description: Australia’s government plans to expand the scope and raise the charges to be imposed on Big Tech companies to encourage them to do deals with local media.
